title: gEndurance: AI-enabled gender-specific behavioral interventions for personalized treatment of chronic diseases
summary:
This study examines how people of different genders use and evaluate digital health services designed to support lifestyle changes. The goal is to identify potential gender-specific differences in the use of so-called smart devices (e.g., smartwatches, smartphone apps). These devices are intended to help patients with type 2 diabetes or high blood pressure improve their lifestyle.
The central question is: To what extent are there differences between the genders in how they use smart devices, how they perceive them, and what effects their use has on their health?
The study is being conducted in several family practices within the Frankfurt Primary Care Research Network. A total of 150 adult patients with type 2 diabetes and/or high blood pressure who own and are able to use a smartphone are participating.
conditions: Health-related lifestyle changes in patients with arterial hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes

interventions.name: The gEndurance project aims to analyze health-related lifestyle changes in patients with arterial hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes mellitus using smart devices, with a focus on gender-specific differences (Phase I data collection). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or arterial hypertension
- Ownership of and ability to use an app-enabled smartphone (requiring at least
iOS 17 or Android 9)
Exclusion criteria:
- Expected life expectancy of less than six months
- Severe cognitive impairments that make independent participation in the
study impossible
- Insufficient knowledge of German, which would make participation in the study
impossible or result in a vocabulary too limited to understand the content of the
study
